source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine – bsi.si / bankart.si / bank domains
why_relevant: Last-resort recovery channel for statistics tables, tariff/fee schedules, ATM/POS network pages and job ads that are routinely deleted after being superseded. Also permits time-series reconstruction of fee and network-size changes that are never published as a series.

source_name: NLB Hackathon 'Odprte finance' – press releases and results
why_relevant: Hackathon briefs state what the bank considers its open-banking/API problem set, and the results release names winning solution themes (financial literacy, PSD2 aggregation). Challenge statements are an unusually candid statement of internal priorities and API capability, published before any product launch.

source_name: Startup.si (SPIRIT/Startup Slovenija) – fintech challenge and event announcements
why_relevant: National startup-ecosystem portal that aggregates corporate challenges, hackathons and accelerator calls issued by banks and payment firms — a pointer source that surfaces bank-sponsored innovation calls this cell would otherwise miss, and identifies emerging fintech counterparties.

source_name: Dnevi slovenske informatike (DSI) – annual conference programme archive
why_relevant: Slovenia's main IT professional conference (32nd edition; per-year subdomains dsi2022…dsi2026 preserve full programmes). Banks, Bankart and their integrators present case studies here with implementation detail and sometimes transaction volumes; the per-year subdomains form a de facto archive of who built what and when. Also runs a student hackathon with ARNES.

source_name: Planet GV – annual conference calendar (finance/tax/controlling)
why_relevant: Major Slovenian professional-event organiser; its annual conference index (incl. the 27th Davcno-financna konferenca, 8-9 Oct 2026, Portoroz) is a pointer to which finance-sector topics get commercial programme slots, and its speaker lists add named practitioners to the actor map. Weaker payments specificity than dpc.delo.si.

source_name: Halcom – Novice (vendor news feed)
why_relevant: Halcom is a long-standing Slovenian e-banking/payment-software vendor to regional banks. Vendor news posts announce bank go-lives, instant-payment and e-signature rollouts, naming client institutions and dates — supplier-side disclosure that usually precedes the bank's own communication.

source_name: Bankart corporate profile deck hosted by ŠC Kranj (third-party mirror)
why_relevant: A company-presentation PDF (prepared for a school career/industry event) mirrored on a third-party education site. Such recruitment-event decks carry operational volume figures and org detail that the corporate site trims, and they survive on the host long after the company withdraws them — an accidental archive.

source_name: Bankart – merchant/technical documentation PDFs (Flik onboarding, versioned)
why_relevant: Bankart publishes dated, version-numbered integration manuals (e.g. Flik onboarding v4.0 March 2024, v4.1 April 2024) under /wp-content/uploads/<year>/<month>/. The version/date sequence is itself a weak signal of scheme change cadence, and superseded versions remain fetchable — a self-archiving directory usable to reconstruct scheme evolution.

source_name: Banka Slovenije Fintech Innovation Hub
why_relevant: The regulator's single point of contact for innovative business models. Any published summaries of hub enquiries, themes or participant categories are an early indicator of which payment innovations are about to enter the Slovenian market, ahead of licensing.

source_name: Slovenian IT/business trade press covering bank innovation (Racunalniske novice, Svet kapitala, Delo Podjetnistvo)
why_relevant: Trade press reports hackathon outcomes, award placements and bank innovation programmes with participant counts and prize funds, and frequently quotes bank executives giving numbers not in official releases. Useful weak-signal amplifier and a route to discovering events that were never announced on a corporate site.

source_name: SiStat podatkovna baza (SURS statistical database, PxWeb)
why_relevant: Master machine-readable repository of every SURS statistical table, including retail turnover, household final consumption (COICOP), ICT/internet use and enterprise online sales. This is the denominator layer for normalising card/POS/ATM payment volumes.

source_name: SiStat PxWeb API help / documentation (Pomoč pri uporabi API-ja)
why_relevant: Documents the exact endpoints, request shapes, rate limits and output formats (PX, CSV, JSON, XLSX, JSON-stat) needed to build a durable automated collector against SiStat, plus the changelog API for update detection.

source_name: SURS StatWeb — Uporaba IKT v gospodinjstvih (ICT usage in households, incl. online shopping and payment methods)
source_subtype: survey programme landing page + First Release series
why_relevant: The annual EU-harmonised ICT household survey is the only official national source for the share of individuals shopping online and, critically, HOW they paid (debit/credit card vs cash on delivery vs bank transfer). Directly measures card-vs-cash behaviour in e-commerce.

source_name: SURS StatWeb — Uporaba IKT v podjetjih / Spletna prodaja (enterprise ICT & online sales)
source_subtype: survey programme (ICT-PODJ, running since 2004) + First Releases
why_relevant: Supply side of e-commerce: share of enterprises selling online and online-sales revenue as % of turnover — the merchant-acceptance denominator for e-commerce acquiring and card-not-present volumes.

source_name: SURS — Trgovina na drobno: prihodek od prodaje (retail trade turnover, monthly)
why_relevant: Monthly and annual retail turnover in value and volume terms is the core denominator for POS transaction value, card penetration of retail spend, and seasonality modelling of terminal throughput.

source_name: SURS — Anketa o porabi v gospodinjstvih (APG / Household Budget Survey)
why_relevant: Detailed household expenditure structure by category, plus savings and indebtedness and durable-goods equipment. Underpins CPI weights and gives the spending basket against which payment-instrument use is normalised.

source_name: SURS — Izdatki gospodinjstev za končno potrošnjo po COICOP 2018 (national accounts table 0301941S)
why_relevant: National-accounts household final consumption expenditure by COICOP purpose, 1995 onwards, current and constant prices. The single most reliable long time series for sizing addressable payment value by spend category.

source_name: SURS — Dohodek, revščina in socialna izključenost (EU-SILC / Življenjski pogoji)
why_relevant: Household disposable income distribution, material deprivation and (in ad-hoc modules) over-indebtedness and financial exclusion — the basis for segmenting who can realistically hold cards/accounts and who remains cash-dependent.

source_name: SURS Release Calendar (Koledar objav / Release calendar)
why_relevant: Publishes in advance the exact date of every one of ~600 annual statistical releases (all releases at 10:30 on working days). Lets a collector be scheduled deterministically rather than polled blindly.

source_name: SURS StatWeb English edition
why_relevant: Full English mirror of SURS releases and metadata — removes translation risk for the analytical layer while remaining the same authoritative dataset. Also hosts the publications catalogue and annual national-statistics reports.

source_name: SURS microdata access for researchers (varna soba / oddaljeni dostop)
why_relevant: Route to individual-level ICT, APG and SILC microdata — the only way to cross-tabulate payment-method use by income, age and region rather than relying on published marginals. Governed by an approval committee (ORA).

source_name: OPSI — Odprti podatki Slovenije (national open data portal)
why_relevant: CKAN-based national catalogue that re-publishes SURS tables (as surs<tableid> datasets) and AJPES registers with stable dataset URIs and machine-readable resources. Excellent discovery layer and a stable alternative access path when stat.si structure changes.

source_name: AJPES — Javna objava letnih poročil (JOLP, public annual reports)
why_relevant: Statutory filing point for all Slovenian companies including banks and payment institutions. Gives audited balance sheets and P&L for acquirers, PSPs, retail chains and ATM operators — the firm-level ground truth behind aggregate payment statistics.

source_name: AJPES — Poslovni register Slovenije (PRS) open data extract
why_relevant: Central register of all Slovenian business entities, partially opened as a twice-monthly XML dump. Enables building a NACE-filtered universe of retailers, payment institutions and e-commerce merchants — the entity backbone for merchant/terminal density analysis.

source_name: AJPES main portal and Katalog informacij javnega značaja
why_relevant: Enumerates every register and public service AJPES operates (PRS, JOLP, eVPO, RNO, statistical surveys), which is the fastest way to discover further structured datasets relevant to merchant and financial-entity mapping.

source_name: UMAR / IMAD — Ekonomsko ogledalo and Poročilo o razvoju
why_relevant: Government macroeconomic analysis office that interprets SURS retail and consumption data monthly, often with commentary and breakdowns published before the underlying tables are easy to assemble. Useful as an early-warning and sense-check layer for consumption-driven payment volumes.

source_name: FURS — Davčno potrjevanje računov (fiscalisation of receipts)
why_relevant: Every cash-business receipt in Slovenia is confirmed in real time by the tax administration, and the legal definition of 'gotovinsko poslovanje' explicitly covers banknotes, coins, payment and credit cards and cheques. If any aggregate of this dataset is published, it is the highest-resolution national proxy for POS transaction counts and cash-vs-card mix.
